To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antiestrogen-ER complexes are more stable than estrogenic-ER complexes, which are in turn more stable than the unliganded ER.
a polyclonal antibody to the ER decreases the binding affinity of estrogens, but not of the antiestrogen tamoxifen, to the ER.
the binding of estrogenic and antiestrogenic ligands to the extranucleaer receptor from human breast tumors can be distinguished by an anti-estrogen receptor antibody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new assay system for the detection of the ER in human breast tumors.

the characterization of the ER from human breast tumors and the development of an antibody to the ER which may be useful for the immunocytochemical localization of the ER and the development of a radioimmunoassay for the ER.
the development of an assay for the extranuclear ER in human breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antiestrogenic activity of MHT is not due to the formation of a complex between the antiestrogen and the ER, and that the antiestrogens are not antagonists of estrogen action at the level of the cytoplasmic receptor.
the antibody to the nuclear ER selectively recognizes the estrogen receptor and not the antiestrogen receptor.
there are important structural differences in the estrogen and antiestrogen complexes of the ER, and that this is a reflection of the different biological actions of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antiestrogenic compound MHT, when bound to the ER, does not appear to induce a conformational change in the ER as does 17 beta-estradiol or DES, and that the antiestrogens do not appear to bind to the same region on the receptor as does the estrogenic ligand.
the binding of anti-estrogens is not affected by anti-ER antibody.
antiestrogens bind to a site on the ER that is different from the site that binds estrogens, and that antiestrogic binding to the ER may not necessarily result in an inactive complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiestrogen MHT binds to a different site on the ER than do the estrogens DES and 17 beta-estradiol.
the antiestrogen MHT does not bind to the ER in the same manner as the estrogenic compounds.
the antiestrogen MHT binds with high affinity to a different conformation of the ER than that of estradiol and DES.
